mention.trail_sentence: This blocking mechanic means that rooms at full capacity force museum-goers to wait, as if in a queue.

items.note: A timing schematic, not a chart: one horizontal axis carrying two schedules, S(u -> v) above and S(v -> w) below, with blue tick bars at the event times and the blocked event printed in red and pointed at by an arrow labelled 'Blocked'. Colour does exactly one job in this diagram - it isolates the single exception on a page of otherwise identical blue marks. Every mark is labelled with a mathematical symbol (t_1^{u->v} ... t_4^{u->v}, t_0^g, t_1 .. t_3^{v->w}) and no axis carries a scale, so the figure is qualitative: it shows the ORDER of events and the one blocked slot, and the times themselves live in the prose. The caption is the paper's only one that defines notation ('S(u -> v) is the schedule for transfers from u to v').

items.note: A 2x2 comparison grid - 4 exits / 8 exits by uniform / variable density - and each panel is a self-contained barcode heat map: ~180 hairline columns (rooms) filled by seconds-until-congested, a printed density ladder down the left edge (0.1 to 0.95 in 0.05 steps) and its own vertical colour bar at the right. Every panel has its own in-art title ('Congestion: 4 Exits, Uniform Density' and so on). The four colour bars are NOT on a common scale - the two top panels run 0-8000, the bottom left runs 0-6000 and the bottom right 0-6000 with coarser ticks - so panels cannot be compared by colour, only by the structure of the blue/yellow/red columns. items.note: The results chart: five setups drawn as overlaid series with translucent fills, 'densities' 0.1-0.9 on x and 'Time for fully evacuate (seconds)' 2k-14k on y, Excel default palette, hairline series lines with no markers, both horizontal and vertical gridlines. Five entries in an unboxed legend outside right. The fills cross rather than stack, so the upper envelope is not a sum - the reader has to follow one colour at a time. In-art title 'Exit Times In Multiple Scenarios' disagrees with the printed caption, and the legend counts SEVEN exits where Figure 8's panels count EIGHT.

note:
## What this paper is

2019 ICM D, team 1908810: "Getting a Move On When the Louvre's Bombed". Three models on one
graph of the Louvre - spectral partitioning of the floor-plan graph, an agent-based
simulation built on queuing theory with an explicit blocking mechanic, and a
differential-flow model over the same adjacency matrix - then sensitivity runs on structural
damage, density distribution and exit count. 20 pages at 612 x 792 pt, 19 printed pages,
18 measured regions, 9 numbered figures and 9 refusals. **No table, no appendix, no deficit.**

## Which section takes which exhibit

- 3.1 opens with **the graph itself** (Figure 1, a force-directed network of ~150 rooms with
  a viridis fill keyed to distance-from-exit).
- 3.4 carries **the partition pair**: a two-panel spectral drawing (Figure 2) and the same
  network re-drawn in 3-D with node size carrying the cut (Figure 3).
- 4.3 carries **the blocking schematic** (Figure 4) - a timing diagram, not a chart - and
  4.4 carries the response-delay chart (Figure 5).
- 5.2 carries **the equilibrium scatter** (Figure 6): one point per room, two reference
  rules at 0.1 and 0.9.
- 6.2 carries **the density pair**: the plan view with the Mona Lisa hotspot (Figure 7) and
  the 2x2 congestion comparison (Figure 8).
- 6.3 carries **the results chart** (Figure 9): five setups, evacuation time against
  density.

So the paper puts a picture next to every modelling claim it makes and a chart next to every
result it reports. The model half (Figures 1-6) holds four drawings and two charts; the
results half (Figures 7-9) holds one drawing and two charts.

## When it goes 3-D

Once, and for one job: Figure 3 is a 3-D projection of the same node-link layout of
Figure 1, used only because a Fiedler cut has to be seen as two SEPARABLE pieces with node
size carrying the split. Nothing else in the paper uses depth - not the timing schematic,
not the 40-bar response-delay chart (flat rectangles at 8x magnification), not the 2x2 heat
quad, not the area chart. Depth here means "this is the same object, seen from above", and
the axes are removed so no scale is claimed for the third dimension.

## Why there is no table at all

The word "Table" never appears in the 20-page text layer. Every number the paper reports
lives in a figure or in prose, and the only ruled boxes on any page are the three algorithm
listings:

| object | shape | why it is not a table |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Algorithm 1 (p8) | boxed, heavy top/bottom, hairline frame verticals, indent guides | one column of free-flowing pseudocode |
| Algorithm 2 (p10) | same, plus a nested indent guide | 'Data:'/'Result:' are inline keyword lines, not header cells |
| Algorithm 3 (p15) | same, split by the layout pass into two measured fragments | one listing; its frame verticals run unbroken across the cut |

Parameter settings that a comparable paper would tabulate (2,532.83 visitors/hour, 7,598.49
people on site, 21,748 safe capacity, 72,737 m2 footprint) are written into a single
paragraph of §4.2. Rule of thumb: **this paper spends its exhibit budget on geometry, not on
grids** - when it needs to show a rule, it draws the mechanism (Figure 4) instead of listing
the cases.

## Caption template

`Figure N:` + sentence-case noun phrase, **the colon is universal (9 of 9)**, the full stop is
not (5 of 9). Length runs 13-22 words, far longer than the lane's usual 5-12, because the
phrase is allowed to be a full descriptive clause: "Figure 6: Node densities that are
experiencing roughly equal in-flow and out-flow are banded in the middle region".

Four captions carry a SECOND sentence, in two flavours. Figures 1 and 4 explain something the
art cannot: Figure 1's "Colors indicate how far a room is from one of the four main exits"
(the colour bar has no key of its own beyond "Connections to nearest exit") and Figure 4's
"S(u -> v) is the schedule for transfers from u to v" (the only caption in the paper that
defines notation). Figures 5 and 9 add the same scope note instead, "Averaged across
simulation trials" - the paper's only statement anywhere about how its numbers were obtained,
and it is printed twice, in captions, never in prose. No caption gives a unit or a condition,
and only Figure 7 states a finding
("highest around the Mona Lisa room"). All 9 print below the art, directly under the
measured region, with no rule between caption and drawing.

## Context connectives

- **"Figure N shows/indicates ..."**: "Figure 2 shows a histogram of values for the vector is
  roughly bimodal" (Figure 2), "Figure 8 indicates baseline densities on the y-axis labels"
  (Figure 8).
- **"In Figure N, ..."**: "In Figure 3, large nodes represent one half of the partition and
  small nodes represent the other half" - the key that the figure itself does not print.
- **"As we see from Figure N, ..."**: "As we see from Figure 9, as the density increases, so
  does the time to fully evacuate".
- **"refer to Figure N"**: "For a visual of the algorithm, refer to Figure 4." The pointer
  sits at the END of §4.3 and the art prints on the next page.
- **"the results shown in Figure 5"**: attached to the end of a simulation paragraph.

Three of the six prose pointers are FORWARD references to art on the next page (Figures 4, 8,
9): the paper names the figure at the bottom of one page and prints it at the top of the
next. Three figures (1, 6, 7) are never named in prose at all; they are introduced by the
sentence that immediately precedes or follows them ("We hand annotated a publicly available
floor plan ... to create a graph", "Plotting the density distribution of all rooms after some
time", "Thus, a more accurate model would take into consideration ...").

Read-backs cluster in the results half: Figure 5 gets three quantified readings (density 0.3
peaks at 5 minutes, 0.65 at 10 minutes, immediate response is fastest), Figure 9 gets two
(more exits shorten the time, more density lengthens it). Figures 1-4 and 6-8 get none.

## Layer defects found in the measured layout

- **Every exhibit is welded to the wrong section.** The layout pass files a region under the
  deepest heading printed BELOW it, and this paper prints 7 of its 9 figures at the top of
  the page (y = 108 of 792). So Figure 1 lands in 3.2 (it introduces 3.1), Figure 4 in 4.4.1
  (it belongs to 4.3), Figure 5 in 5.2 (it is the last exhibit of 4.4), Figure 6 in 6.1 (it
  closes 5.2), Figure 8 in 6.3 (it belongs to 6.2) and Figure 9 in 7.3 (it belongs to 6.3).
  Only Figures 2, 3 and 7 land in the right section, and only because their section happens
  to be the next heading on the page. All nine records were re-assigned by the rule "the
  section is the one whose prose introduces or reads the exhibit".
- **Algorithm 1 is welded FORWARD to §4** (it prints in §3.5), and Algorithm 2 to §4.4.1 (it
  prints in §4.3): the same forward-walk, applied to a non-exhibit.
- **Algorithm 3 is measured as two regions** with the header line of the listing appearing
  in both crops; the frame verticals run unbroken across the gap, so the listing is one
  object that the region pass cut. Filed as two refusals, not two exhibits.
- **Figure 8 is measured as four regions**, one per panel, with no region over the whole 2x2
  block. The record anchors on panel 1 and files r2-r4 as fragments.
- **The caption detector truncates Figure 7**: the layer reports "highest around the" and
  drops "Mona Lisa room." because the art's own annotation interrupts the run. The caption
  is quoted from the text layer by slicing to the printed full stop.
- **The footer counts 19 pages while the file has 20** ("Page 4 of 19" prints on PDF page 5);
  two headings repeat in the TOC rows and are dropped from every section path.

## Declared deficits

None. All 9 printed captions have a measured region, all 18 regions are accounted for, and
the four panels of Figure 8 and the two panels of Figure 2 are each measured separately. This
is the first paper in the lane where no exhibit is unmeasured - the interesting fact is the
inverse one: **the paper prints no table at all**, so there is nothing to miss.
rules: Not one table in 19 printed pages: the word 'Table' never appears in the text layer, and the only ruled boxes on any page are the three algorithm listings, which are one-column framed pseudocode with indent guides, not grids. [caption.numbering]

Exhibits go to the TOP of the page: 7 of 9 figures sit at y=108 of 792, so the paper names a figure at the foot of one page and prints it at the head of the next - Figures 4, 8 and 9 are all forward references with a one-page lead. [place.page_zone]

Section membership has to be taken from the prose, not from the page: because the figure prints above the heading that introduces it, the layout pass files six of the nine figures one or two subsections late (Figure 1 in 3.2, Figure 5 in 5.2, Figure 9 in 7.3). [place.section_path]

The pictures do the model's work and the charts do the results': the model half (3-5) holds a force-directed network, a spectral pair, a binding-time schematic and one bar chart, while the sensitivity and results sections (6-7) hold one plan view, one heat quad and one area chart. [geometry.family]

One chart type per job and never a second: histogram-plus-curve for the spectral cut (Figure 2), grouped bars for response delay (Figure 5), open-circle scatter for equilibrium (Figure 6), barcode heat strips for congestion (Figure 8), area series for evacuation time (Figure 9). [geometry.family]

Depth is used exactly once, on the SAME node-link layout that is drawn flat elsewhere, and only because a cut has to be seen as two separable pieces; the 40-bar chart, the 2x2 heat quad and the area chart are all flat. [geometry.three_d]

Legends are rare and always outside right: 2 of 9 figures carry one (the two Excel-style result charts, Figures 5 and 9), unboxed, five chips, no title; the model-half drawings are keyed by an in-art title or by the prose sentence beside them instead ('large nodes represent one half of the partition'). [geometry.legend]

Colour bars appear twice and are never shared: Figure 1 keys a viridis fill to a single vertical bar (0-12, 'Connections to nearest exit'), while Figure 8 gives each of its four panels its OWN bar and the scales differ (0-8000 in the top row, 0-6000 below), so the quad can be compared by pattern but not by colour. [geometry.colorbar]

Colour is spent on the exception, once per figure: the red bar among blue ones in Figure 4 marks the blocked event, the single magenta line in Figure 2 marks the cut, the one saturated yellow room in Figure 7 marks the Mona Lisa hotspot. Everything else in those drawings is a single neutral or a single hue. [geometry.legend]

No mark in the paper is annotated with a value: 6 of 9 figures print numeric ticks, but data labels are absent everywhere - the only text inside a drawing is a title, an axis name, or the words 'Mona Lisa'. [geometry.data_labels]

Seven of the nine figures print their own title inside the drawing ('Graph Layout of The Louvre', 'Density by Room', 'Exit Times In Multiple Scenarios', the four 'Congestion: 4 Exits, Uniform Density' panel titles), so the caption is a second, longer title rather than the only one - and on Figure 9 the two titles disagree. [caption.verbatim]

Caption template is 'Figure N:' with the colon on 9 of 9, a sentence-case noun phrase of 13-22 words, and a full stop on only 5 of 9; the phrase is allowed to be a descriptive clause ('Node densities that are experiencing roughly equal in-flow and out-flow are banded in the middle region'). [caption.numbering]

Four captions carry a second sentence: two explain what the art cannot (Figure 1's colour key, Figure 4's notation) and two are the same scope note, 'Averaged across simulation trials', printed on Figures 5 and 9 - the only place the paper says how the numbers were obtained. The explanatory pair is the paper's whole substitute for a legend. [caption.sentences]

Captions stay neutral: no units, no conditions, one variable (Figure 4's S(u -> v)) and one finding (Figure 7's 'highest around the Mona Lisa room'). Every other caption names the thing and stops. [caption.concludes]
All 9 captions print below the art, flush under the measured region, with no rule between caption and drawing - the caption is separated from the body by whitespace alone. [caption.position]

Six of nine figures are named in prose and three (Figures 1, 6, 7) never are: the unnamed ones are carried entirely by the sentence above or below them, so an exhibit can be introduced without ever printing its number. [mention.first_page]

The lead form varies but the number never leaves the lead: 'Figure 2 shows ...', 'In Figure 3, ...', 'For a visual of the algorithm, refer to Figure 4.', 'obtain the results shown in Figure 5', 'Figure 8 indicates ...', 'As we see from Figure 9, ...'. No parenthetical '(Fig. 5)' anywhere. [mention.lead_pattern]

Read-backs are quantified and confined to the results half: three for Figure 5 (density 0.3 peaks at 5 minutes, 0.65 at 10, immediate response fastest) and two for Figure 9 (more exits shorten, more density lengthens); the model half gets a pointer and no reading. [mention.read_sentences]

Only two multi-panel recipes are used and both are comparison devices: a 1x2 row with a shared x scale (Figure 2) and a 2x2 quad of self-contained panels (Figure 8). There is no before/after arrow pair, no inset and no faceted column. [geometry.panel_layout]

No exhibit takes more than 14% of its page and none is a solo page: the largest is Figure 3 at 0.141, the smallest the top-left panel of Figure 8 at 0.038, so the paper keeps room for prose beside every drawing. [place.area_frac]
